headline_marked: [[Iran captures US underwater drone]], plans reverse-engineering; US Navy claims it was defective
headline: Iran captures US underwater drone, plans reverse-engineering; US Navy claims it was defective
summary: Iranian forces recovered a 19-foot Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle near the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian embassies are openly mocking the US, suggesting immediate reverse-engineering efforts.
details: Iran has captured a U.S. Navy underwater drone near the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian forces reportedly planning to reverse-engineer the vehicle. The U.S. Navy, however, claims the lost Anduril Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle was defective and unclassified.

The 19-foot Dive-LD drone malfunctioned while surveying regional waters before being recovered by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Iranian embassies globally are openly mocking the U.S., with one posting about an 'Unboxing ceremony by our reverse engineers, tomorrow morning!'

Anduril, the drone's manufacturer, promotes the Dive-LD as a highly reliable and adaptable vehicle capable of operating for up to 10 days. This contrasts with the Navy's description of it as an 'older, defective model' that 'neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment.'

Washington has historically taken similar incidents seriously, as seen when Iran recovered an RQ-170 Sentinel stealth reconnaissance drone in 2011. Tehran subsequently claimed to have reverse-engineered that aircraft, influencing its domestic drone designs.

Experts suggest Iranian engineers could 'definitely reverse-engineer the mechanical systems' of the captured drone. However, they are more skeptical about Tehran's ability to penetrate the software, which reportedly includes defenses against exploitation.

Regardless of technical success, analysts believe Iran will exploit the incident for propaganda, framing it as evidence of U.S. ineptitude. This narrative aims to assert Iranian control over the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.
